A domain expert states a rule; the model has to put it somewhere. This page is the vocabulary arclint and the domain-librarian skill use to place it: the definitions, recordings, and checks come from the Domain-Driven Design meta-model arclint carries (`arclint domain`), the questions are the ones the skill asks, and every code sample is quoted from a worked example under `docs/examples`: the Go example compiles and passes its tests, and both examples pass `arclint check`. A rule id such as `invariant/enforced-at-every-mutation` is a built-in rule; `arclint rules <id>` prints it in full.

## Business rule is an intake word

A rule of the business as a domain expert states it, before the model has placed it. Once placed it is an invariant, when it must hold at all times for an aggregate or a value; an assertion, when it is a guarantee of one command of a root or one operation of a domain service; a specification, when experts pass the predicate around as a thing they name; or not a domain rule, when it is a programming guard or an application policy such as notifying or exporting. It is an intake word and is never recorded as its own section. [[1]](#ref-1)[[2]](#ref-2)[[3]](#ref-3)[[4]](#ref-4)[[5]](#ref-5)

Recorded as an invariant, an assertion, or a specification with one owner, or left unrecorded as an application policy or a guard.

- **Fundamental.** A rule that holds only when one operation runs is recorded as an assertion on that operation, in the expert's words; a rule that spans aggregates and must hold at every instant has no owner and is a question for the domain expert. [[1]](#ref-1)[[6]](#ref-6)

## Rules: where a rule lives

A rule the model has placed is one of three things. Each is recorded under the owner that keeps it true, and each names the method that checks it.

### Invariant

A consistency rule that must hold whenever the objects it constrains can be observed: an aggregate's invariants hold at the end of every operation on the aggregate, and a value object's invariants hold for every value that exists. The aggregate root, or the value object's constructor, is responsible for enforcing it, so that a state violating it is never reachable. In the code an invariant is stated as an assertion. [[7]](#ref-7)[[1]](#ref-1)[[5]](#ref-5)

**Recorded under** `invariants`. A map from key to statement, recorded under the aggregate or value object that owns it; the owner is the nesting, never a reference.

| Property | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | yes | The rule's name in kebab-case, unique within its owner and stable across edits: it is how a finding, a suppression, and a baseline refer to the rule. For an aggregate's invariant it also names the root method that enforces it: ensure followed by the key, spelled in the language's method case, so lines-frozen is enforced by EnsureLinesFrozen in Go, ensureLinesFrozen in TypeScript, and ensure_lines_frozen in Python. |
| `statement` | yes | The rule in the ubiquitous language, as a domain expert would state it. |

| Rule | What holds | Checked |
|---|---|---|
| `invariant/owned-by-aggregate-or-value-object` | An invariant is owned by exactly one recorded aggregate or value object; an invariant written under a member entity, an event, or under nothing, is rejected. [[7]](#ref-7)[[1]](#ref-1) | when the domain file loads |
| `invariant/keyed-within-owner` | Every invariant carries a kebab-case key, unique within its owner and distinct from the owner's assertion keys; the parser rejects a key recorded twice under one owner, and the loader rejects an empty key or an empty statement. [[1]](#ref-1)[[5]](#ref-5) | when the domain file loads |
| `invariant/key-names-the-rule` | An invariant's key names the rule it protects, in the ubiquitous language; a key that names only the act of checking (validate, check, verify, is-valid, check-rules, ensure, assert, guard) is rejected, because a name that describes the means says nothing about the effect. [[8]](#ref-8)[[9]](#ref-9) | when the domain file loads |
| `invariant/enforced-at-every-mutation` | Every constructor and every command of the root calls the ensure method of the aggregate's invariant, so the invariant is evaluated at the completion of every state-mutating operation and a violation fails the operation; a root with no constructor has no door at which to enforce it. [[7]](#ref-7)[[10]](#ref-10) | by `arclint check` |

- **Fundamental.** Model true invariants in consistency boundaries; a rule that can tolerate a delay is not an invariant of the aggregate and belongs to eventual consistency outside it. [[7]](#ref-7)[[5]](#ref-5)
- Report a refused operation under the name of the rule that refused it, so that the interface tells which rule failed without a trace through the implementation. [[8]](#ref-8)
- Keep the rule's logic on the aggregate or value object that owns it; a model whose objects are bags of getters and setters, with the rules pushed out to services, is anemic and has none of the benefits of a domain model. [[3]](#ref-3)[[7]](#ref-7)

### Assertion

A stated post-condition of an operation or invariant of a class or aggregate, made explicit so that the effect of an operation can be known without tracing its implementation. Assertions define the contracts of services and entity modifiers and the invariants on aggregates; where they cannot be coded directly, they are written as automated unit tests. [[1]](#ref-1)[[11]](#ref-11)[[12]](#ref-12)

**Recorded under** `assertions`. A map keyed by the assertion's name, recorded under the aggregate whose command it constrains or under the domain service whose operation it constrains; the assertions of a service are its contract.

| Property | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | yes | The assertion's name in kebab-case, unique within its owner; the owner's method that checks it is assert followed by the key, spelled in the language's method case (AssertHasLines, assertHasLines, assert_has_lines). |
| `on` | yes | The operation the guarantee belongs to: a command of the root, or an operation of the service. |
| `statement` | yes | The guarantee as the domain expert states it, in the ubiquitous language (Only an active tenant offers an invitation); it is recorded in the expert's words and never rewritten into a post-condition, because on already names the operation. |

| Rule | What holds | Checked |
|---|---|---|
| `assertion/names-owner-operation-and-check` | An assertion carries a statement, names the operation it constrains, and carries a key naming the method that checks it. [[1]](#ref-1) | when the domain file loads |
| `assertion/owned-by-an-aggregate-or-service` | An assertion is recorded under one aggregate or one domain service; an assertion under a value object, a member entity, or nothing is rejected. [[1]](#ref-1) | when the domain file loads |
| `assertion/checked-by-its-operation` | The owner of an assertion, the aggregate's root or the domain service, declares both the operation the assertion names and the checking method (assert followed by the key in the language's method case), and the operation calls the checking method. [[13]](#ref-13)[[1]](#ref-1) | by `arclint check` |

- **Fundamental.** State post-conditions of operations and invariants of classes and aggregates explicitly; where they cannot be coded directly, write automated unit tests for them. [[1]](#ref-1)
- Seek models with coherent sets of concepts that lead a developer to infer the intended assertions. [[1]](#ref-1)[[14]](#ref-14)

### Specification

A predicate-like value object that tells whether a candidate object matches some criteria, separating the statement of what kind of objects can be selected from the object that does the selecting. It answers through one operation, isSatisfiedBy, and can be combined with other specifications. [[15]](#ref-15)[[2]](#ref-2)

**Recorded under** `specifications`.

| Property | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | The specification's name, the name of its type in the code; the map key. |
| `definition` | yes | The criteria it states, in the ubiquitous language. |

| Rule | What holds | Checked |
|---|---|---|
| `specification/satisfaction-method` | A specification is a declared type carrying a satisfaction method (SatisfiedBy, satisfiedBy, or satisfied_by). [[15]](#ref-15) | by `arclint check` |

## Behavior: which operation carries it

A rule is checked by an operation. These are the operations a model and the application around it are built from, and the one record of what they did.

### Command

An operation of an aggregate root that changes the state of that one aggregate and returns no domain information, named for what it does in the ubiquitous language. It is never a setter, and it is never the request a use case receives. [[16]](#ref-16)[[17]](#ref-17)

**Recording:** A command has no entry of its own; its name is the `on` of the assertions recorded under its aggregate.

- **Fundamental.** Keep commands very simple and let them return no domain information; the logic they rely on belongs in queries, which have no side effects. [[16]](#ref-16)

### Query

An operation of an aggregate or a value object that returns a result and changes no observable state; Evans calls it a side-effect-free function. No operation is both a query and a command. [[16]](#ref-16)[[17]](#ref-17)

**Recording:** A query is not recorded; a predicate experts name and pass around is recorded as a specification instead.

- **Fundamental.** Place as much of the logic as possible into queries, operations that return results with no observable side effects. [[16]](#ref-16)

### Domain Service

A standalone operation in the domain for a significant process or transformation that is not a natural responsibility of an entity or value object, given a name that is part of the ubiquitous language and a contract stated as assertions. It makes a business decision that no one aggregate or value can make alone; it may read through repositories, but it never commits and never publishes. [[13]](#ref-13)[[18]](#ref-18)[[19]](#ref-19)[[20]](#ref-20)

**Recorded under** `services`. A map keyed by the service's name; its assertions are its contract, each on one operation of the service.

| Property | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | The service's name, the name of its type in the code; the map key. |
| `definition` | yes | The business decision it makes and across which aggregates. |
| `assertions` | no | The service's contract: a map keyed by the assertion's name, each with on (the operation of the service) and statement, checked by the service's method assert followed by the key in the language's method case. |

| Rule | What holds | Checked |
|---|---|---|
| `domain_service/declared` | A recorded service is a declared type spelled with the service's name in the language's type case. [[13]](#ref-13) | by `arclint check` |
| `domain_service/not-held-by-aggregates` | No aggregate root or member entity declares a field whose type is a recorded domain service; a service reaches an aggregate only as a parameter of one command. [[21]](#ref-21)[[22]](#ref-22) | not yet; waits for the `field-types` milestone |

- **Fundamental.** Try the thing first; a service exists only for a business decision that no entity or value object naturally owns, and the more behavior the services hold, the less the model does. [[13]](#ref-13)[[3]](#ref-3)
- **Fundamental.** Name the service and its operations for their effect and purpose in the ubiquitous language, never for the means; a name ending in Manager, Helper, Handler, or Processor names no effect. [[13]](#ref-13)[[8]](#ref-8)
- A service holds collaborators (repositories, other services, a clock) and never state that survives an invocation; Evans no longer holds statelessness to be necessary, and Vernon's services hold repositories. [[18]](#ref-18)[[23]](#ref-23)[[24]](#ref-24)
- Use a domain service for an operation that spans aggregates; look up what it needs ahead of invoking aggregate behavior, and pass a service into a command only for a dependency resolution the aggregate itself must double-dispatch. [[23]](#ref-23)[[25]](#ref-25)

### Application Service

An operation of the application layer that runs one use case flow: it translates the request into domain values, fetches aggregates through repositories, invokes their commands or one domain service, commits, and publishes what happened, holding application logic that is not business logic and never the domain rules themselves. Use case is the same thing seen from the request; the two words are not two kinds. [[26]](#ref-26)[[27]](#ref-27)[[3]](#ref-3)[[28]](#ref-28)[[29]](#ref-29)

**Recording:** Application services are the use cases of the application Zone in rules.arclint.yaml; the domain file does not record them, and a business rule found in one is a finding for the librarian, not an entry.

- **Fundamental.** Keep it thin; it coordinates tasks and delegates work to domain objects, contains no business rules or knowledge, and holds no state reflecting the business situation. If deleting every step it takes would lose a business decision, that decision belongs to an aggregate or a domain service. [[3]](#ref-3)[[26]](#ref-26)
- Notifying, exporting, retrying, and transaction control are application logic, sometimes called workflow logic; they belong here and are never recorded as domain rules. [[4]](#ref-4)
- Name the use case for the action it performs, and name its input type for the request (ProvisionTenantRequest), never with the word command, which names a state-changing operation of a root. [[28]](#ref-28)[[17]](#ref-17)

### Domain Event

A full-fledged part of the domain model representing something that happened in the domain that domain experts care about, as distinct from a system event. It is ordinarily immutable, being a record of the past, and typically carries the time it occurred and the identities of the entities involved. [[30]](#ref-30)[[31]](#ref-31)[[32]](#ref-32)

**Recorded under** `events`. A map keyed by the event's name.

| Property | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | The event's name, the name of its type in the code, phrased as something that happened; the map key. |
| `definition` | yes | What happened and who cares. |
| `raised_by` | no | The aggregate whose operation raises it. |

| Rule | What holds | Checked |
|---|---|---|
| `domain_event/raised-by-an-aggregate` | An event that records what raises it names an aggregate of its own context; an event raised by a value object, a service, or a name the context does not record is rejected. [[30]](#ref-30)[[33]](#ref-33) | when the domain file loads |
| `domain_event/declared` | A recorded event is a declared type spelled with the event's name in the language's type case. [[30]](#ref-30) | by `arclint check` |
| `domain_event/no-setters` | An event declares no method whose name begins with set; a record of the past is not edited. [[30]](#ref-30)[[31]](#ref-31)[[34]](#ref-34) | by `arclint check` |
| `domain_event/occurrence-time` | An event declares a field carrying the time it occurred. [[30]](#ref-30)[[31]](#ref-31)[[34]](#ref-34) | not yet; waits for the `field-declarations` milestone |
| `domain_event/immutable` | Every field of an event is immutable after construction. [[30]](#ref-30)[[31]](#ref-31) | not yet; waits for the `field-mutability` milestone |

- Name an event in the past tense for what happened, and name a time point clearly for which time it is, occurrence or notice. [[31]](#ref-31)[[35]](#ref-35)
- **Fundamental.** Ignore irrelevant domain activity; make explicit the events the domain experts want to track or be notified of, or which are associated with state change in other model objects. [[30]](#ref-30)

## Where each rule lives

The example column quotes the worked example's `domain.arclint.yaml`; the Go and TypeScript columns name the method each language spells for it, read from the example's code.

| The rule is | Recorded as | Lives on | Checked by | In the example | Go | TypeScript | Built-in rules |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| invariant of a value | `invariants` under the value object | value object | its constructor, the one door | `TenantName`: `length-within-bounds` | `NewTenantName` | `TenantName.from` | `value_object/constructed-through-one-door` |
| invariant of a cluster | `invariants` under the aggregate | aggregate root | `Ensure` and the key, called by every constructor and command | `Tenant`: `one-open-invitation-per-description` | `EnsureOneOpenInvitationPerDescription` | `ensureOneOpenInvitationPerDescription` | `aggregate/invariants-enforced-by-root`<br>`invariant/enforced-at-every-mutation` |
| assertion on a command | `assertions` under the aggregate, `on` the command | aggregate root | `Assert` and the key, called by that command | `Tenant`: `invites-only-while-active` on `OfferRegistrationInvitation` | `AssertInvitesOnlyWhileActive` | `assertInvitesOnlyWhileActive` | `assertion/checked-by-its-operation` |
| assertion on a service operation | `assertions` under the domain service, `on` the operation | domain service | `Assert` and the key, called by that operation | `TenantProvisioningService`: `tenant-active-on-completion` on `ProvisionTenant` | `AssertTenantActiveOnCompletion` | `assertTenantActiveOnCompletion` | `assertion/checked-by-its-operation` |
| specification | `specifications` | its own type | `SatisfiedBy` | the example records none |  |  | `specification/satisfaction-method` |
| delivery policy: notify, export, retry, commit | not recorded | application service, or a subscriber to a domain event | plain code | publishing the events after the unit of work | `Execute` | `execute` |  |
| programming guard: a nil check, a parse failure | not recorded | the code that needs it | plain code |  |  |  |  |

The application service is the one place a rule never lives: keep it thin; it coordinates tasks and delegates work to domain objects, contains no business rules or knowledge, and holds no state reflecting the business situation. If deleting every step it takes would lose a business decision, that decision belongs to an aggregate or a domain service. [[3]](#ref-3)[[26]](#ref-26)

## Provisioning a tenant, top to bottom

The worked example is the identity and access context of Vernon's *Implementing Domain-Driven Design*, written twice: in Go under `docs/examples/go` and in TypeScript under `docs/examples/ts`, from one `domain.arclint.yaml`. Provisioning a tenant touches every word above.

### 1. The application service runs the use case

`ProvisionTenant` translates the request into domain values, runs the domain service inside one unit of work, and publishes the events the aggregates raised. It makes no business decision of its own.

`identityaccess/provisiontenant/provision_tenant.go`

```go
// Execute runs the use case flow.
func (uc *ProvisionTenant) Execute(ctx context.Context, req ProvisionTenantRequest) (Outcome, error) {
	name, err := tenant.NewTenantName(req.TenantName)
	if err != nil {
		return Outcome{}, fmt.Errorf("provision tenant: %w", err)
	}
	fullName, err := user.NewFullName(req.AdministratorFirstName, req.AdministratorLastName)
	if err != nil {
		return Outcome{}, fmt.Errorf("provision tenant: %w", err)
	}
	email, err := user.NewEmailAddress(req.AdministratorEmailAddress)
	if err != nil {
		return Outcome{}, fmt.Errorf("provision tenant: %w", err)
	}

	var provisioned provisioning.Provisioned
	err = uc.unit.Run(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) error {
		var err error
		provisioned, err = uc.service.ProvisionTenant(ctx, name, req.TenantDescription, provisioning.Administrator{Name: fullName, Email: email})
		return err
	})
	if err != nil {
		return Outcome{}, err
	}
	if err := uc.publisher.Publish(ctx, provisioned.Events); err != nil {
		return Outcome{}, fmt.Errorf("provision tenant %s: publish events: %w", provisioned.TenantID, err)
	}
	return Outcome{TenantID: provisioned.TenantID, AdministratorID: provisioned.AdministratorID, InitialPassword: provisioned.InitialPassword}, nil
}
```

`src/identityaccess/provision-tenant/provision-tenant.ts`

```ts
async execute(request: ProvisionTenantRequest): Promise<Outcome> {
  const name = TenantName.from(request.tenantName);
  const fullName = FullName.of(request.administratorFirstName, request.administratorLastName);
  const email = EmailAddress.from(request.administratorEmailAddress);

  const provisioned = await this.unit.run(() => this.service.provisionTenant(name, request.tenantDescription, { name: fullName, email }));
  await this.publisher.publish(provisioned.events);
  return { tenantId: provisioned.tenantId, administratorId: provisioned.administratorId, initialPassword: provisioned.initialPassword };
}
```

### 2. The domain service makes the decision that spans aggregates

Provisioning creates a Tenant, a User, and a Role together, which no one of them can do alone. The service's contract is the assertions recorded under it:

`domain.arclint.yaml`

```yaml
TenantProvisioningService:
  definition: >-
    Brings a tenant into existence with its Administrator role and
    its first administrator, registered through a one-time
    invitation; spans Tenant, User, and Role.
  assertions:
    administrator-registered:
      on: ProvisionTenant
      statement: A provisioned tenant has an enabled user in its Administrator role.
    initial-invitation-withdrawn:
      on: ProvisionTenant
      statement: Nobody else registers through the invitation the first administrator used.
    tenant-active-on-completion:
      on: ProvisionTenant
      statement: A provisioned tenant is active.
```

`identityaccess/provisioning/tenant_provisioning_service.go`

```go
// ProvisionTenant brings a tenant into existence with its Administrator
// role and first administrator, registered through a one-time invitation.
//
// Contract (assertions on ProvisionTenant):
//   - tenant-active-on-completion
//   - administrator-registered
//   - initial-invitation-withdrawn
func (s *TenantProvisioningService) ProvisionTenant(ctx context.Context, name tenant.TenantName, description string, admin Administrator) (Provisioned, error) {
	if existing, err := s.tenants.TenantNamed(ctx, name); err == nil && existing != nil {
		return Provisioned{}, fmt.Errorf("provision tenant %q: %w", name, tenant.ErrTenantNameTaken)
	} else if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, tenant.ErrTenantNotFound) {
		return Provisioned{}, fmt.Errorf("provision tenant %q: %w", name, err)
	}

	t, err := tenant.Provision(s.tenants.NextIdentity(), name, description, s.clock)
	if err != nil {
		return Provisioned{}, err
	}
	invitation, err := t.OfferRegistrationInvitation(initialInvitation)
	if err != nil {
		return Provisioned{}, err
	}

	adminUser, password, err := s.registerAdministrator(t, invitation, admin)
	if err != nil {
		return Provisioned{}, err
	}
	if err := t.WithdrawInvitation(invitation.InvitationID()); err != nil {
		return Provisioned{}, err
	}

	adminRoleName, err := role.NewRoleName(AdministratorRoleName)
	if err != nil {
		return Provisioned{}, err
	}
	adminRole, err := role.Provision(t.TenantID(), adminRoleName, "Default tenant administrator.", s.clock)
	if err != nil {
		return Provisioned{}, err
	}
	if err := adminRole.AssignUser(adminUser.UserID()); err != nil {
		return Provisioned{}, err
	}

	if err := s.AssertTenantActiveOnCompletion(t); err != nil {
		return Provisioned{}, err
	}
	if err := s.AssertAdministratorRegistered(t, adminUser, adminRole); err != nil {
		return Provisioned{}, err
	}
	if err := s.AssertInitialInvitationWithdrawn(t); err != nil {
		return Provisioned{}, err
	}

	if err := s.tenants.Add(ctx, t); err != nil {
		return Provisioned{}, fmt.Errorf("provision tenant %q: %w", name, err)
	}
	if err := s.users.Add(ctx, adminUser); err != nil {
		return Provisioned{}, fmt.Errorf("provision tenant %q: %w", name, err)
	}
	if err := s.roles.Add(ctx, adminRole); err != nil {
		return Provisioned{}, fmt.Errorf("provision tenant %q: %w", name, err)
	}

	events := append(t.Events(), adminUser.Events()...)
	events = append(events, adminRole.Events()...)
	return Provisioned{
		TenantID:          t.TenantID(),
		AdministratorID:   adminUser.UserID(),
		AdministratorRole: adminRole.RoleID(),
		InitialPassword:   password,
		Events:            events,
	}, nil
}
```

`src/identityaccess/provisioning/tenant-provisioning-service.ts`

```ts
/**
 * Contract (assertions on provisionTenant):
 * tenant-active-on-completion, administrator-registered, initial-invitation-withdrawn.
 */
async provisionTenant(name: TenantName, description: string, admin: Administrator): Promise<Provisioned> {
  if ((await this.tenants.tenantNamed(name)) !== undefined) {
    throw new TenantNameTaken(name);
  }
  const tenant = Tenant.provision(this.tenants.nextIdentity(), name, description, this.clock);
  const invitation = tenant.offerRegistrationInvitation(INITIAL_INVITATION);

  const { user: adminUser, password } = this.registerAdministrator(tenant, invitation, admin);
  tenant.withdrawInvitation(invitation.invitationId);

  const adminRole = Role.provision(tenant.tenantId, RoleName.from(ADMINISTRATOR_ROLE_NAME), "Default tenant administrator.", this.clock);
  adminRole.assignUser(adminUser.userId);

  this.assertTenantActiveOnCompletion(tenant);
  this.assertAdministratorRegistered(tenant, adminUser, adminRole);
  this.assertInitialInvitationWithdrawn(tenant);

  await this.tenants.add(tenant);
  await this.users.add(adminUser);
  await this.roles.add(adminRole);

  return {
    tenantId: tenant.tenantId,
    administratorId: adminUser.userId,
    administratorRole: adminRole.roleId,
    initialPassword: password,
    events: [...tenant.drainEvents(), ...adminUser.drainEvents(), ...adminRole.drainEvents()],
  };
}
```

Each assertion is checked by a method named `assert` and the key, and the operation calls it:

`identityaccess/provisioning/tenant_provisioning_service.go`

```go
// AssertTenantActiveOnCompletion checks the contract assertion
// tenant-active-on-completion on ProvisionTenant: the provisioned tenant
// is active.
func (s *TenantProvisioningService) AssertTenantActiveOnCompletion(t *tenant.Tenant) error {
	if !t.IsActive() {
		return fmt.Errorf("tenant %s: %w", t.TenantID(), ErrTenantLeftInactive)
	}
	return nil
}
```

`src/identityaccess/provisioning/tenant-provisioning-service.ts`

```ts
/** Checks the contract assertion tenant-active-on-completion on provisionTenant. */
assertTenantActiveOnCompletion(tenant: Tenant): void {
  if (!tenant.isActive()) {
    throw new Error(`tenant ${tenant.tenantId.toString()}: provisioning left the tenant inactive`);
  }
}
```

### 3. The aggregate checks its commands

The Tenant records one invariant and one assertion:

`domain.arclint.yaml`

```yaml
Tenant:
  definition: >-
    A subscribing organisation that owns users and roles; it is
    active from provisioning until deactivated, and while active it
    offers registration invitations that users register through.
  identity: TenantID
  entities:
    RegistrationInvitation:
      definition: >-
        An invitation, identified within its tenant, through which a
        user registers; it is open-ended or limited to a window.
  invariants:
    one-open-invitation-per-description: >-
      No two invitations of a tenant that are available at the same
      moment carry the same description.
  assertions:
    invites-only-while-active:
      on: OfferRegistrationInvitation
      statement: Only an active tenant offers a registration invitation.
  repository: TenantRepository
```

Offering an invitation is a command: it changes the tenant and is named for what it does. It checks the assertion first and the invariant last.

`identityaccess/tenant/tenant.go`

```go
// OfferRegistrationInvitation opens a new open-ended invitation under the
// given description and returns it.
func (t *Tenant) OfferRegistrationInvitation(description string) (RegistrationInvitation, error) {
	if err := t.AssertInvitesOnlyWhileActive(); err != nil {
		return RegistrationInvitation{}, err
	}
	invitation, err := newRegistrationInvitation(description)
	if err != nil {
		return RegistrationInvitation{}, err
	}
	if t.IsRegistrationAvailableThrough(invitation.Description()) {
		return RegistrationInvitation{}, ErrInvitationAlreadyOffered
	}
	t.invitations = append(t.invitations, invitation)
	if err := t.EnsureOneOpenInvitationPerDescription(); err != nil {
		return RegistrationInvitation{}, err
	}
	return invitation, nil
}
```

`src/identityaccess/tenant/tenant.ts`

```ts
/** Opens a new open-ended invitation under the description. */
offerRegistrationInvitation(description: string): RegistrationInvitation {
  this.assertInvitesOnlyWhileActive();
  const invitation = RegistrationInvitation.offer(description);
  if (this.isRegistrationAvailableThrough(invitation.description)) {
    throw new Error("an available invitation with that description already exists");
  }
  this.invitations.push(invitation);
  this.ensureOneOpenInvitationPerDescription();
  return invitation;
}
```

`identityaccess/tenant/tenant.go`

```go
// AssertInvitesOnlyWhileActive checks the assertion invites-only-while-active
// on OfferRegistrationInvitation and LimitInvitation: an invitation is
// offered or limited only by an active tenant.
func (t *Tenant) AssertInvitesOnlyWhileActive() error {
	if !t.active {
		return fmt.Errorf("tenant %s: %w", t.tenantID, ErrTenantInactive)
	}
	return nil
}
```

`src/identityaccess/tenant/tenant.ts`

```ts
/**
 * Checks the assertion invites-only-while-active on offerRegistrationInvitation
 * and limitInvitation: an invitation is offered or limited only by an active tenant.
 */
assertInvitesOnlyWhileActive(): void {
  if (!this.active) {
    throw new Error(`tenant ${this.id.toString()} is not active`);
  }
}
```

Deactivating the tenant carries no assertion, but like every command it ends by calling the invariant's ensure method:

`identityaccess/tenant/tenant.go`

```go
// Deactivate takes the tenant out of use; every user of the tenant loses
// access until it is activated again.
func (t *Tenant) Deactivate() error {
	if !t.active {
		return ErrTenantAlreadyInactive
	}
	t.active = false
	if err := t.EnsureOneOpenInvitationPerDescription(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	t.Raise(TenantDeactivated{TenantID: t.tenantID, occurredOn: t.clock()})
	return nil
}
```

`src/identityaccess/tenant/tenant.ts`

```ts
deactivate(): void {
  if (!this.active) {
    throw new Error("tenant is already inactive");
  }
  this.active = false;
  this.ensureOneOpenInvitationPerDescription();
  this.recorder.raise(new TenantDeactivated(this.id, this.clock()));
}
```

`identityaccess/tenant/tenant.go`

```go
// EnsureOneOpenInvitationPerDescription enforces the aggregate invariant
// one-open-invitation-per-description: a tenant holds at most one
// available registration invitation per description.
func (t *Tenant) EnsureOneOpenInvitationPerDescription() error {
	now := t.clock()
	seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(t.invitations))
	for _, invitation := range t.invitations {
		if !invitation.IsAvailable(now) {
			continue
		}
		if _, dup := seen[invitation.Description()]; dup {
			return fmt.Errorf("tenant %s: %w: %q", t.tenantID, ErrInvitationAlreadyOffered, invitation.Description())
		}
		seen[invitation.Description()] = struct{}{}
	}
	return nil
}
```

`src/identityaccess/tenant/tenant.ts`

```ts
/**
 * Enforces the aggregate invariant one-open-invitation-per-description:
 * a tenant holds at most one available registration invitation per description.
 */
ensureOneOpenInvitationPerDescription(): void {
  const now = this.clock();
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  for (const invitation of this.invitations) {
    if (!invitation.isAvailable(now)) {
      continue;
    }
    if (seen.has(invitation.description)) {
      throw new Error(`tenant ${this.id.toString()}: two available invitations share the description "${invitation.description}"`);
    }
    seen.add(invitation.description);
  }
}
```

### 4. A query answers without changing anything

Whether a user may register through an invitation is a query; the command above asks it before it changes anything.

`identityaccess/tenant/tenant.go`

```go
// IsRegistrationAvailableThrough is a side-effect-free function: it
// answers whether a user may register through the identified invitation
// right now.
func (t *Tenant) IsRegistrationAvailableThrough(identifier string) bool {
	index := t.invitationIndex(identifier)
	return index >= 0 && t.invitations[index].IsAvailable(t.clock())
}
```

`src/identityaccess/tenant/tenant.ts`

```ts
/** Side-effect-free: whether a user may register through the identified invitation now. */
isRegistrationAvailableThrough(identifier: string): boolean {
  const invitation = this.invitations.find((i) => i.isIdentifiedBy(identifier));
  return invitation !== undefined && invitation.isAvailable(this.clock());
}
```

### 5. A value keeps its own invariant at its one door

`TenantName` records the invariant `length-within-bounds`. Its constructor is the only way to make one, so no tenant name outside the bounds exists.

`identityaccess/tenant/tenant_name.go`

```go
// NewTenantName is the one door through which text becomes a TenantName.
// Invariant length-within-bounds: the trimmed name is 1 to 100 characters.
func NewTenantName(text string) (TenantName, error) {
	trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(text)
	if trimmed == "" {
		return TenantName{}, ErrTenantNameBlank
	}
	if utf8.RuneCountInString(trimmed) > 100 {
		return TenantName{}, ErrTenantNameTooLong
	}
	return TenantName{value: trimmed}, nil
}
```

`src/identityaccess/tenant/tenant-name.ts`

```ts
/** The one door: invariant length-within-bounds, the trimmed name is 1 to 100 characters. */
static from(text: string): TenantName {
  const trimmed = text.trim();
  if (trimmed === "") {
    throw new Error("tenant name must not be blank");
  }
  if ([...trimmed].length > 100) {
    throw new Error("tenant name must be at most 100 characters");
  }
  return new TenantName(trimmed);
}
```

### 6. An event records what happened

Provisioning raises `TenantProvisioned`. The aggregate raises it; the application service publishes it after the unit of work completes.

`identityaccess/tenant/events.go`

```go
// TenantProvisioned records that a new tenant came into existence; the
// provisioning use case and the billing context care.
type TenantProvisioned struct {
	TenantID   TenantID
	Name       TenantName
	occurredOn time.Time
}
```

`src/identityaccess/tenant/events.ts`

```ts
/** A new tenant came into existence; provisioning and billing care. */
export class TenantProvisioned implements DomainEvent {
  constructor(readonly tenantId: TenantID, readonly name: TenantName, readonly occurredOn: Date) {}
}
```

### 7. A rule with no owner is a question

No two tenants share a name, but no one tenant owns that rule, so it is not recorded as an invariant. It stays an open question for the domain expert until they answer it:

`domain.arclint.yaml`

```yaml
questions:
  tenant-name-uniqueness: >-
    No two tenants share a name, but no single tenant owns that rule.
    When a tenant's name is registered, what else must change in the
    same transaction? If nothing, the rule is recorded as an assertion
    of TenantProvisioningService on ProvisionTenant.
```

## The questions that decide

When the input does not say where a rule lives, the domain-librarian skill asks rather than guesses. Its policy: Ask the single question that unblocks; batch only when several concepts block at once; never ask what the input already answers.

### When the input is not enough

| Question | Decides | Defined by |
|---|---|---|
| Does <X> have an identity that survives attribute changes, or are two <X> with the same values interchangeable? | entity vs value_object | Entity [[36]](#ref-36)[[18]](#ref-18)[[37]](#ref-37)<br>Value Object [[38]](#ref-38)[[39]](#ref-39)[[18]](#ref-18)[[40]](#ref-40) |
| What must never be violated about <X>, even for an instant? | invariants and owner |  |
| Does <rule> hold even while nothing runs, or only when <operation> runs? | invariant vs assertion | Invariant [[7]](#ref-7)[[1]](#ref-1)[[5]](#ref-5)<br>Assertion [[1]](#ref-1)[[11]](#ref-11)[[12]](#ref-12) |
| Which operation guarantees <rule>, and who performs it: one aggregate, or a process that spans aggregates? | assertion owner (aggregate vs domain_service) | Aggregate [[7]](#ref-7)[[41]](#ref-41)[[42]](#ref-42)[[43]](#ref-43)<br>Domain Service [[13]](#ref-13)[[18]](#ref-18)[[19]](#ref-19)[[20]](#ref-20) |
| Does <X> change anything, or does it only answer a question? | command vs query | Command [[16]](#ref-16)[[17]](#ref-17)<br>Query [[16]](#ref-16)[[17]](#ref-17) |
| Can one <Aggregate> do <X> with what it already holds, or does <X> need another aggregate or knowledge none of them holds? | command vs domain_service | Command [[16]](#ref-16)[[17]](#ref-17)<br>Domain Service [[13]](#ref-13)[[18]](#ref-18)[[19]](#ref-19)[[20]](#ref-20) |
| Is <X> a result the business names, or a step the software takes to deliver one? | domain_service vs application_service | Domain Service [[13]](#ref-13)[[18]](#ref-18)[[19]](#ref-19)[[20]](#ref-20)<br>Application Service [[26]](#ref-26)[[27]](#ref-27)[[3]](#ref-3)[[28]](#ref-28)[[29]](#ref-29) |
| Do experts pass this predicate around as a thing they name, rather than as a rule that simply holds? | specification vs invariant or assertion | Specification [[15]](#ref-15)[[2]](#ref-2)<br>Invariant [[7]](#ref-7)[[1]](#ref-1)[[5]](#ref-5)<br>Assertion [[1]](#ref-1)[[11]](#ref-11)[[12]](#ref-12) |
| Is this a property of the value itself (constructor) or of the cluster that must stay consistent on every command? | value integrity vs cluster invariant |  |
| Would you say this to an expert who never saw the language? | domain contract vs programming-only guard |  |
| When <X> changes, what else must change in the same transaction? | aggregate boundary |  |
| Does the business care about <X>'s lifecycle (created, changed, closed)? | entity vs value_object vs domain_event | Entity [[36]](#ref-36)[[18]](#ref-18)[[37]](#ref-37)<br>Value Object [[38]](#ref-38)[[39]](#ref-39)[[18]](#ref-18)[[40]](#ref-40)<br>Domain Event [[30]](#ref-30)[[31]](#ref-31)[[32]](#ref-32) |
| Which people/teams use the term <X>, and do they mean the same thing? | bounded_context assignment | Bounded Context [[44]](#ref-44)[[45]](#ref-45)[[46]](#ref-46)[[47]](#ref-47) |

### When the input conflicts with the record

| Question | Decides | Defined by |
|---|---|---|
| <X> is already defined as <def> in context <C>: (a) same concept, (b) different concept needing its own context, or (c) a correction? | reuse vs split vs update |  |
| This change breaks invariant <rule> owned by <owner>. Is the invariant wrong, or is this a different concept? | revision vs new term |  |

### Distillation rules

The rules the skill applies to turn what an expert said into recorded terms.

| Rule | States | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `identity-test` | Concept keeps its business identity while attributes change -> entity. | order keeps its number when status changes |
| `value-test` | Two instances with identical values are interchangeable -> value_object. | any two USD 10 amounts are the same money |
| `invariant-ownership` | First establish a domain consistency rule and its capable owner; must-always/must-never wording alone does not establish one. Contributor workflow, host guarantees, delivery validation and programming guards are not automatically invariants or assertions. A justified rule holding at all observable times -> the owner's invariants, keyed; a justified guarantee of a named domain operation -> the owner's assertions, keyed, with on: the aggregate's for its command, the domain service's for its operation. A value object's key names value integrity checked at construction; an aggregate's key names the root method that enforces the cluster rule. | total = sum of lines -> Order.invariants.total-is-sum-of-lines; every tier priced before Publish -> Order.assertions.tiers-priced on Publish |
| `specification-as-thing` | Experts pass the predicate around as a thing -> specifications, a type with SatisfiedBy; never a flag on a value object and never an invariant. | preferred customer is handed to pricing as a spec, not inlined as a must-always |
| `language-not-guards` | Record only what you would say to an expert who never saw the language; programming-only guards are not domain contracts. | nil receiver check is not an invariant; a Price is never negative is |
| `transaction-boundary` | Smallest cluster consistent in one transaction -> one aggregate; everything else by ID, eventually. | reject: customer and all orders save together |
| `thing-first` | A behavior goes to the entity or value that naturally owns it before any service is considered; a service that could be a method on one root is a wrong home. | Tenant.Deactivate, not TenantService.Deactivate(tenant) |
| `command-vs-query` | Changes the state of one aggregate and returns no domain information -> a command of that root; changes nothing and answers a question -> a query of the root or value; never both in one operation. Neither is recorded. | Tenant.Deactivate is a command; Tenant.IsRegistrationAvailableThrough is a query |
| `domain-service-when-no-owner` | Does it make a business decision that no one aggregate can make alone? Yes -> domain_service, recorded under services with its contract; it may read through repositories, never commits, never publishes. | TenantProvisioningService over Tenant, User, and Role; Encrypter for knowledge no aggregate holds |
| `application-service-holds-no-rule` | If I delete every step here, is any business decision lost? No -> application_service: loading, invoking, committing, publishing, notifying, translating; not recorded. Yes -> the decision is placed under its owner and reported as a finding. | the ProvisionTenant use case runs the service in one unit of work and publishes; it holds no rule |
| `contract-of-a-service` | A guarantee of one operation of a domain service -> the service's assertions, keyed, with on naming the operation; the set is the service's contract. | TenantProvisioningService.assertions.tenant-name-unique on ProvisionTenant |
| `precondition-as-assertion` | A rule that holds only when one named command runs, not at every instant -> the owner's assertions with on that command; the statement stays as the expert said it and is never rewritten into a post-condition. | Tenant.assertions.invites-only-while-active on OfferRegistrationInvitation, not a Tenant invariant, because a deactivated tenant is legal |
| `not-a-domain-rule` | A promise about delivery (notify, export, retry, transaction control) or a programming guard -> no entry; the application service or the code does it. | notify billing on TenantProvisioned is a subscriber, not an assertion |
| `intention-revealing-name` | Name a service and its operations for effect and purpose in the ubiquitous language, never for the means; a name ending in Manager, Helper, Handler, or Processor is a finding to rename, not a kind. An application service's input is named for the request, never with the word command. | TenantProvisioningService.ProvisionTenant, not TenantManager.Handle; ProvisionTenantRequest, not ProvisionTenantCommand |
| `event-detection` | State change experts say in past tense -> domain_event; technical changes are not events. | OrderConfirmed yes, RowUpdated no |
| `context-split` | Same word, materially different meaning per team -> separate bounded_contexts + relation. | Product: price in Catalog, weight in Shipping |
| `language-fidelity` | Record terms exactly as experts say them; reject developer jargon. | policy renewal, not ContractUpdateManager |
| `synonym-collapse` | One meaning, one canonical term per context; synonyms become aliases. | client/customer/account -> customer |
| `repository-gate` | Repositories only for aggregate roots; inner entity wanting one = wrong boundary. | reject OrderLineRepository; reject "we must list comps, so Comp is a root" |
| `minimal-evidence` | Classify on the fewest deciding facts; two plausible kinds -> ask, never guess. | 'we track shipments' alone decides nothing -> ask |
